text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose slightly today, continuing a sharp rebound from last week's dip. The move reflects a broader recovery in refining conditions: US crude is trading around $90 per barrel, refineries are running at 95% capacity, and heating oil prices remain elevated—up 59% from last winter—which supports margins on refined products like diesel and heating fuel that the company produces.

The stock's climb from $373 to $415 over the past week also sits against a backdrop of tightening global oil supply relative to demand. Though Russian crude production has recovered and global markets are moving toward surplus, the spike in heating oil prices shows real demand pressure heading into winter, which benefits a large refiner with significant heating oil production.
